From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Hanna Li <hanna@finsentry.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T13:05:00Z
Subject: Technical follow-up — auth, routing, embeddings & reranker notes

Hi Hanna — following up with more technical detail so your infra team can preliminarily review. High-level answers plus concrete examples below.

1) Auth patterns (Okta + mTLS)- Option A: Okta-issued short-lived tokens exchanged by backend service; Redwood SDK accepts bearer tokens and enforces per-token routing policies.
- Token rotation: we support 1h refresh tokens and key rotation via your KMS.
- mTLS: we can run mutual TLS at the private deployment edge (if on-prem/VPC) — we'll provide cert templates and a sample NGINX ingress config.

2) SDK setup (snippets & SDK flavors)- JS (browser + Node) and Python examples in the checklist. Quick Node snippet: 

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'open-redwood-medium-v1', prompt: '...' });

We will provide Okta login flow with a short-lived RW token for client-facing apps and recommend doing any secret calls from server-side.

3) Routing & availability- Region pinning: per-tenant configuration; fallback to nearest compatible region if pinned region is saturated.
- Model-tier routing: policy-based routing (latency SLO vs cost).
- Latency bands (example): open-redwood-small (p50 45ms, p95 220ms), open-redwood-medium (p50 85ms, p95 380ms) — we'll measure during workshop with your sequences.

4) Embeddings & reranker- Recommend 1536 dimensions (float16/quantized variants supported). Storage: vector DB (we support connectors to Pinecone/FAISS/Snowflake).
- Reranker flow: embeddings -> ANN recall (top-200) -> distilled reranker (small LM) re-ranks top-10. This reduces token compute and improves precision.

5) Structured output / tool calling- We support schema-constrained generation (validate/output JSON) and explicit tool-calls. Example: 

System: You are an extractor. Output EXACT JSON schema: {"invoice_number":"string", "total":"number"} 
User: [invoice text]

If a tool-call is returned (TOOL_CALL search), the client receives a structured token with method and args and can execute it.

6) Prompt governance & injection mitigation (brief)- Versioning: prompts stored with immutable IDs and semantic tags (v1, v1.1), diffable histories, and promoted to production via canary deploys.
- Guardrails: response schema validation, token-level allowlists/denylists, and model-level safety filters.
- Injection mitigations: input sanitization, meta-prompting that sets immutable system instructions, and output validation.
- Red-team: we provide a starter red-team playbook and a set of adversarial prompt templates for internal testing.

I'll attach a compact spreadsheet with recommended settings for embeddings/rerankers and a short NGINX mTLS snippet in the checklist. Let me know which items you want expanded before the workshop.

Best,
Neha
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: finsentry-arch-notes.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Technical follow-up — auth, routing, embeddings & reranker notes

Hanna — great, glad the workshop slot works. Two quick items from a governance/process perspective and a small deliverable we're attaching for your review.

Prompt governance proposal (short):
- Prompt artifacts: store prompt text + metadata (author, immutable id, schema expectations, tags, last-run eval metric).
- Versioning & rollout: edit -> stage -> canary (10% traffic) -> promote. Every change creates an audit entry with who deployed and which eval prompt set was used.
- Prompt injection defenses: (1) enforce system-level immutable instructions, (2) sanitize user-provided content, (3) run adversarial prompt tests annotated as part of CI for prompt changes.
- Red-team cadence: recommend initial cycle during integration phase (2 weeks), then quarterly for production prompts. We'll provide a starter set of adversarial templates and scoring rubric.

Attached: prompt-template-v1.json — this is a small schema-guided template for structured extraction + meta fields for versioning. Use it as a working example: it includes a "schema" field, a "version_id", and an example of allowed substitutions.

Log retention & audit notes: we keep prompt history and alert on quality regressions tied to a prompt change. For enterprise/private deployments we can align retention windows and export audit logs to your SIEM.

Proposed next actions
- We (Redwood) will send the workshop invite for Tue 2026-11-30 14:00 PT and include a short pre-read (architecture checklist + prompt template).
- FinSentry: confirm attendee list and an initial set of 10 prompts you want us to include in the red-team exercise.

If this looks good I'll have legal coordinate on the retention language with your team.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
